gloss: small birds (swallows and sparrows); petty person

definitions.explanation: A literary term combining the characters for swallow ({燕|つばめ}) and sparrow ({雀|すずめ}), collectively referring to small, common birds.

definitions.gloss: a person of small ambition; a petty person
definitions.explanation: Used figuratively to refer to someone with limited vision or small aspirations, as contrasted with someone of great ambition or stature. Derives from the famous proverb about swallows and sparrows not understanding the ambitions of the great roc.

examples.japanese: ⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{木|き}→木：00524_ki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{燕雀|えんじゃく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{集|あつ}まっていた→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧。
examples.english: Small birds had gathered in the garden tree.

examples.japanese: {燕雀|えんじゃく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{群|む}れ→群れ：00298_mure⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{空|そら}→空：02216_sora⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{飛|と}び{交|か}う⟦{季節|きせつ}→季節：01304_kisetsu⟧になった。
examples.english: The season has come when flocks of small birds fly back and forth across the sky.

examples.japanese: {燕雀|えんじゃく}⟦いずく→いずい：07551_izui⟧んぞ{鴻鵠|こうこく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{志|こころざし}→志：06655_kokorozashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{知|し}らん→知る：00458_shiru⟧や。
examples.english: How could swallows and sparrows ever know the ambition of the great roc?
examples.notes: The most famous use of this word, from the Chinese historical text Records of the Grand Historian.

examples.japanese: {燕雀|えんじゃく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦あの{人|ひと}→あの人：25922_anohito⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{大志|たいし}→大志：28925_taishi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{理解|りかい}→理解：03674_rikai⟧⟦できまい→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: Small-minded people couldn't possibly understand that person's great ambition.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{周囲|しゅうい}→周囲：03206_shuui⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{燕雀|えんじゃく}たち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{嘲笑|ちょうしょう}→嘲笑：09026_choushou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{気|き}→気：02199_ki⟧にせず、⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{夢|ゆめ}→夢：01519_yume⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{追|お}い→追う：02016_ou⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧た。
examples.english: He continued to pursue his dream, unbothered by the mockery of the small-minded people around him.

examples.english: Even while knowing I was just an ordinary person, I worked toward a grand goal.

notes:
A literary compound of {燕|えん} (swallow) and {雀|じゃく} (sparrow). Primarily encountered in the famous proverb and in elevated writing.

FAMOUS PROVERB:
{燕雀|えんじゃく}⟦いずく→いずい：07551_izui⟧んぞ{鴻鵠|こうこく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{志|こころざし}→志：06655_kokorozashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{知|し}らん→知る：00458_shiru⟧や — "How could swallows and sparrows know the ambitions of the great roc?" From the Chinese historical text ⟦{史記|しき}→史記：29596_shiki⟧ (Records of the Grand Historian) by Sima Qian. Used to express that ordinary people cannot comprehend the aspirations of the truly ambitious.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {燕雀|えんじゃく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{徒|と} — people of petty ambition
- {鴻鵠|こうこく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{燕雀|えんじゃく} — the great and the small; those of high ambition versus the ordinary

RELATED WORDS:
- {鴻鵠|こうこく} — great roc; metaphor for a person of grand ambition (the counterpart to {燕雀|えんじゃく})
- ⟦{大志|たいし}→大志：28925_taishi⟧ — great ambition
- {小人|しょうじん} — a petty or small-minded person

REGISTER:
Highly literary and formal. Used almost exclusively in writing, speeches, or quotations. Understanding this word is valuable for reading classical Japanese and Chinese-influenced literature.
